rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
